title: Pet psychic says animals tell her their owners' secrets - and cats are worst
excerpt: The 'medialist' says dogs and cats are very open when they tell her about what their owners get up to
content:
The 'medialist' says dogs and cats are very open when they tell her about what their owners get up to

Neil Shaw Assistant Editor (Money and Lifestyle)

10:26, 26 Nov 2026

Emma Dawn was fascinated when she saw a professional ‘animal communicator’ speak to her dogs, and decided it was a career she wanted to follow. A hairdresser at the time, the 45-year-old retrained and now speaks to animals — both dead and alive.

‌

‌

Emma, from East Riding, Yorkshire, was already ‘medialistic’, meaning she speaks to spirits by switching off her conscious mind, letting her subconscious come into play. “I open my mind and get messages mostly through picture form, as well as short videos,” Emma said. “But I am also able to feel any symptoms that the animals have. So if they are in any discomfort I can tell you where that is.”

‌

Emma’s says her speaking to animals has been verified with vets, who say her diagnosis is usually correct. But it’s not just health issues Emma can pick up from animals — they can talk about their owners too. “I always ask owners if they have any secrets their animals are going to share. The pets can tell me anything.

Article continues below

“Dogs are the worst for sharing their secrets. They can tell me about people sneaking food when they are dieting and hiding it from their family and partners, they tell me about people that have come to the house, they can tell me anything.

“Always be careful around your animals, they take everything in and they hear everything. Animals can hear us humans, I just have the ability to communicate back to them and hear them.”

Emma says rescue animals always give her vivid and memorable stories about their past lives. “This rescue dog described to me that it had been rescued from a hole that was full of snakes,” she said. “The owner then told me that was exactly what had happened.”

‌

Her favourite animals to connect with are horses, as they look at the world in a completely different way and the energy they give off is a lot more similar to humans. “The most mischievous animals are cats. They’re the ones I have to work the hardest with as they don’t want to give anything away. It takes a while for them to trust you.

“I once had a cat that told me the complete opposite to every answer to a question to make me look wrong,” Emma recalled. “They can also be quite insulting and ginger cats are the worst for that. I remember getting this message and thinking how I was going to tell the owner what the cat had just told me. Wondering if I should just sugarcoat it or not as I didn’t want to offend anyone.

‌

‌

“The cat had told me that their owner needed to change their fashion sense. They didn’t like the clothes they wore and that the colours didn’t go with their hair. That was a really interesting one.” But while Emma is confident she can bridge the communication gap between pets and their owners, she does run into the odd sceptic.

“Some people are curious about what I do, while others say that I make it all up and just take people’s money for the sake of it. People believe what they want to believe. You have people that don’t believe in mediumship either, even though it’s been proven time and time again. Some people just want things in black and white.”

‌

Before a reading, Emma will always ask a pet to give them evidence: asking the animal to tell her something only they and their owner know, so that when she relays the information, the owner knows she truly has got it from their pet.

“People will look at me and wonder how I know that. I would never do a reading unless I proved the evidence because I don’t want people to ever question if I am just making stuff up.”

‌

‌

Before she starts, Emma will always ask owners for a list of questions, while also giving the pet the opportunity to ask her questions too. “I just try and have a conversation with them and drop questions in. For a lot of animals, once you get them talking, they’re just like children — they just carry on and there is no filter. It means you can get shown anything.”

Emma aims for 45-minute-long conversations, but says if an animal was in full flow, she’d never cut them off as she believes it’s therapeutic for them. “Imagine living in a country and you don't speak their language. And then, all of a sudden, you find someone that speaks English. All of a sudden, this person understands you, so you might want to just get everything out.”

‌

Emma recalls one conversation she had with a rescue dog, trying to figure out where his problematic behaviour was coming from. The dog told her about his previous life trying to survive on the streets, and that he had once been stabbed.

“This dog really wasn’t keen on other dogs,” she says. “Dogs are generally the happiest, so sometimes you really have to dig deep to find a root cause of a problem with a dog as they are very good at masking. They want you to think that they’re happy.”

‌

‌

Owners will contact Emma for a number of reasons, including if their pet seems happier or more upset than usual, if they become more reactive towards things or if they think there may be a problem. “They come to me and then I can get to the root cause of it. Something it can be as simple as being reactive because their harness is rubbing. Then the owner will get them a new one and the dog is back to being happy as Larry.

“I spoke to someone else whose dog seemed really unhappy, and it turned out it was because their son had gone to university and the dog was missing him.”

But while she can communicate with other people’s pets, it’s not as easy for her when it comes to her own dogs. “I think there is a boundary put up there when it comes to my pets, I just can’t seem to get to them.”
